message.content:
**Uno – Quick‑Start Rules** | Section | What Happens | |---------|--------------| | **Goal** | Be the first player to score 500 points (or whatever you agree on). Points are earned by being the first to finish each round. | | **Setup** | • 108‑card deck (standard Uno deck).
• Each player draws 7 cards.
• Place the remaining cards face down to form the draw pile.
• Turn the top card of the draw pile face up to start the discard pile. If it’s an action card, follow its effect before play begins. | | **Turn Order** | Players take turns clockwise (unless a reverse card changes direction). | | **Playing a Card** | On your turn you may play one card that matches either the **color** or the **number/symbol** of the top card on the discard pile.
• **Wild** cards (wild, wild draw four) can be played at any time and let you choose the new color. | | **Action Cards** | • **Skip** – next player loses their turn.
• **Reverse** – changes play direction.
• **Draw Two** – next player draws two cards and loses their turn.
• **Wild Draw Four** – next player draws four cards and loses their turn; you may only play this if you have no other playable card (otherwise you risk a challenge). | | **Drawing a Card** | If you cannot play a card, you must draw one from the draw pile. If that card is playable, you may play it immediately; otherwise, your turn ends. | | **Calling “Uno”** | When you have **exactly one card left**, you must say “UNO!” before the next player takes their turn. If you forget and another player catches you, you must draw two penalty cards. | | **Winning a Round** | The round ends when a player discards all their cards. That player scores points equal to the sum of the values of the cards remaining in opponents’ hands:
• Number cards = face value.
• Skip/Reverse/Draw Two = 20 points.
• Wild/Wild Draw Four = 50 points. | | **Scoring** | Add the round score to the winner’s total. Play continues until someone reaches the target score (usually 500). | --- ### Quick Tips 1. **Keep track of colors** – If you’re low on cards, try to keep a variety of colors so you can always play something. 2. **Use Wilds strategically** – Save them for when you’re stuck or to change the color to your advantage. 3. **Watch opponents** – If someone says “UNO,” they’re about to win; be ready to play a counter‑action if possible. 4. **Challenge Wild Draw Four** – If you suspect the previous player had a playable card, you can challenge. If they were wrong, they draw four; if they were right, you draw six. Enjoy playing Uno!
